project.title: VulnScan
project.description: Language-agnostic dependency vulnerability scanner CLI written in Go, querying OSV.dev to detect and score known vulnerabilities across Go, npm, and Python projects.
resume_points: Built a stdlib-only Go CLI that detects project ecosystems and parses Go, npm, and Python dependency manifests.
Integrated the OSV.dev API for batch vulnerability queries and implemented a CVSS v3.1 base-score calculator from scratch.
Designed a concurrent worker-pool scanner with context-based cancellation, an on-disk TTL cache, and offline scan mode.
Built a pluggable Parser/Provider architecture so new ecosystems and vulnerability databases can be added without touching core logic.

details.architecture: Stdlib-only Go CLI: a detector walks the project tree to identify ecosystems, self-registering Parser implementations extract dependencies, a worker-pool scanner queries pluggable vulnerability Providers (OSV.dev) concurrently, and results are scored and rendered via terminal/JSON/Markdown/CSV reporters.
details.challenges: Designing a CVSS v3.1 base-score calculator from the raw vector spec for advisories that ship a vector but no pre-bucketed severity, and building an extensible Parser/Provider interface so new ecosystems and databases are additive, not invasive.
details.security: Scans dependency manifests against known-vulnerability data (OSV.dev), computes severity and a security score per project, and generates remediation commands as a review-before-you-run script rather than auto-applying fixes.
details.improvements: Planned: Rust/Java/.NET/PHP/Ruby/Docker/Terraform ecosystem parsers, additional providers (GHSA, NVD), SARIF/HTML output, SBOM generation (CycloneDX/SPDX), typosquat/malicious-package detection, and CI templates.

project.title: jgateway
project.description: Production-grade reverse proxy / API gateway in Go with a composable middleware pipeline — auth, rate limiting, request signing, circuit breaking, and retries, all wired from a single declarative config.
resume_points: Built a data-driven reverse proxy in Go with a composable middleware chain, keeping the core proxy dumb and all cross-cutting behavior in independently testable middleware.
Implemented pluggable auth (JWT + API key, fail-closed), a spoof-resistant token-bucket rate limiter, and HMAC request signing with constant-time comparison.
Built resilience primitives from scratch: idempotency-aware retries with jittered exponential backoff, and a per-upstream circuit breaker (closed/open/half-open).
Added structured logging, Prometheus metrics, liveness/readiness health checks, fail-fast config validation, and graceful shutdown with in-flight request draining.

details.architecture: Stdlib-only Go (net/http, httputil.ReverseProxy, slog). Longest-prefix router dispatches to per-upstream handlers built from a YAML-defined middleware chain: logging, metrics, auth, rate limit, signing, retry, circuit breaker, wrapped in a top-level panic-recovery middleware.
details.challenges: Designing a middleware contract where ordering dependencies are explicit and safe (e.g. auth before rate-limiting-by-identity) while keeping every middleware independently unit-testable via httptest, with no shared global state.
details.security: Auth fails closed on any validation error; API keys and HMAC signatures use constant-time comparison; rate-limit keys avoid trusting client IP unless explicitly configured behind a trusted LB; secrets are sourced only from env vars, never hardcoded or logged.
details.improvements: Planned: OpenTelemetry tracing hooks, Redis-backed rate-limit store for multi-instance deployments, govulncheck + golangci-lint wired into CI.

project.title: 6502 Emulator
project.description: Cycle-counted MOS 6502 CPU emulator in C++17 with a flat 64KB memory bus, memory-mapped I/O and timer devices, and an interactive command-line debugger/monitor.
resume_points: Built a cycle-accurate MOS 6502 CPU emulator in C++17, passing Klaus Dormann's official 6502_functional_test.bin opcode test suite.
Implemented a 256-entry opcode dispatch table covering all 56 official mnemonics across 12 addressing modes.
Designed memory-mapped I/O and timer peripherals (modeled on an ACIA/UART and 6522 VIA) with real hardware-interrupt delivery.
Built an interactive command-line debugger/monitor supporting stepping, breakpoints, and live memory/register inspection.

details.architecture: A flat 64KB Bus intercepts fixed-address console and timer registers before falling through to plain RAM; the CPU core drives fetch-decode-execute via a 256-element opcode table of addressing-mode/instruction function pointers, calling Bus::tick() each step to advance the timer.
details.challenges: Getting non-blocking keyboard input into a running emulated program without stalling emulation speed -- polling every instruction dropped a 96-million-instruction test run from under a second to minutes, so input is instead polled via a real syscall (_kbhit) every 4096 instructions.
details.security: Not a security-focused project; the ROM-region write-protect (setRomRegion) and automatic I/O-region disabling on loads that overlap memory-mapped device addresses are the closest analogues, guarding against a runaway program clobbering ROM or misinterpreting device registers as data.
details.improvements: Planned: broader illegal-opcode coverage and 65C02 extended-opcode support (currently unsupported, per the Klaus Dormann 65C02 test suite).
